title: Charred Corn, Cherry Tomato & Avocado Salad with Seared Fish
description: A bright summer salad of charred sweet corn, cherry tomatoes, avocado, scallions, cilantro, and seared mild white fish with a lime, cumin, paprika, and chile vinaigrette.
ingredients: 320 g fresh corn kernels, about 2 large ears
50 g scallions, thinly sliced, white and pale green parts
300 g ripe but firm avocado flesh, sliced, about 2 large avocados
15 g fresh cilantro, roughly chopped, plus a few sprigs for garnish
680 g firm mild white fish, preferably mahi mahi; halibut, cod, or sea bass also work
5 g garlic, about 1 clove, finely grated or mashed
2 g cumin seed, toasted and ground
2 g piment d'Espelette or cayenne, plus more to taste
52 g fresh lime juice, divided, plus more to taste
135 g extra virgin olive oil, divided
steps: Make the vinaigrette: mash the garlic with a pinch of kosher salt. Stir in the ground cumin, paprika, piment d'Espelette, and about 38 g of the lime juice. Whisk in about 105 g of the olive oil until combined. Taste and adjust with salt, lime, or chile as needed.

Char the corn: heat a large cast iron skillet, sauté pan, or Blackstone over high heat until very hot. Add the corn in a relatively even layer and cook, tossing only occasionally, until the kernels are tender-crisp with scattered dark brown char, about 3 to 5 minutes. Transfer to a bowl and let cool for a few minutes.

Add the cherry tomatoes and scallions to the charred corn. Season lightly with salt and toss with just enough vinaigrette to coat without making the salad heavy. Taste and adjust with additional lime or salt.

Pat the fish very dry and cut into roughly 4 to 5 cm pieces. Season with kosher salt and a light dusting of paprika or piment d'Espelette. Heat the remaining olive oil in a large skillet over high heat and sear the fish until browned outside and just cooked through, turning as little as possible. Cook to 145°F / 63°C at the thickest point if checking with a thermometer.
Transfer the fish to a bowl and gently toss with the remaining lime juice and a spoonful of the vinaigrette.

Arrange the avocado slices on four plates and season them lightly with salt. Fold the chopped cilantro into the corn and tomato mixture, then spoon the salad around and partly over the avocado. Tuck the seared fish throughout the salad, drizzle with any remaining vinaigrette, and finish with cilantro sprigs. Serve immediately.
notes:
Fish options:
Mahi mahi — first choice here. Mild, slightly sweet, and firm enough to develop a good sear without falling apart.
Halibut — clean, firm, and excellent with the lime and corn, though usually pricier.
Cod — very good and affordable, but more delicate; keep the pieces larger and turn them carefully.
Sea bass — richer and slightly more luxurious, which plays well against the bright lime dressing.

The original inspiration used briefly cooked corn. This version intentionally chars the corn instead for more depth while keeping the kernels crisp and sweet.
